title: Symmetric vs asymmetric encryption trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for symmetric-vs-asymmetric-encryption trace events.

keys.description: Every key in the lab. The whole topic is readable from this list: how many keys an algorithm needs, and which of them may be published.

kind.description: secret = one shared symmetric key; public/private = the two halves of a pair.

bits.description: Key length. Not comparable across families - 256 symmetric bits are far stronger than 2048 asymmetric ones.

owner.description: Who a key pair belongs to; empty for a shared secret, which has no single owner.

holders.description: Who has these bytes. A symmetric key needs at least two holders to be useful; a private key must have exactly one.

published.description: True only for a public half, where being published is the purpose rather than a leak.

compromised.description: The key reached somebody it should not have.

operation.description: The step just performed: what went in, which key was used, what came out.

name.description: generate, publish, encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, wrap key, unwrap key, share, intercept, leak, compare, count keys, tamper, report.

family.description: Which kind of cryptography this step used.

keyId.description: The key this step was performed with.

keyKind.description: secret, public or private - which half was used, since that is what selects the guarantee.

micros.description: Model cost of this operation in microseconds: proportional to data for symmetric, flat and large for asymmetric.

verdict.description: blocked = the attacker could not proceed, which is a success for the system.

channel.description: Everything that has travelled over the wire so far.

family.description: key-material = a key itself sent in the clear; signature = a readable message plus a proof of authorship.

label.description: What the payload is - the plaintext, or a file name for a sized blob.

onTheWire.description: What an observer actually sees. Equal to the label when nothing was encrypted.

keyId.description: The key that opens or verifies this entry.

wrappedKey.description: The session key encrypted to the recipient's public key; set only for hybrid envelopes.

intact.description: False once the payload was changed in flight.

readableBy.description: Who can turn this back into plaintext right now - recomputed after every key event, so a leak retroactively widens it.

attacker.description: What the party on the path has collected.

holds.description: Key ids the attacker has. Published public keys are always here, which is the point: having them helps nothing.

seen.description: Messages observed on the wire, readable or not.

keyManagement.description: How many keys a group of this size needs under each scheme.

parties.description: Zero until a comparison has been requested.

secretKeys.description: n(n-1)/2 - one shared secret per pair, growing quadratically.

keyPairs.description: n - one pair per party, growing linearly, with every public half publishable.

cost.description: What the run has spent, plus the most recent hypothetical comparison.

comparison.description: A what-if for one payload: symmetric in one pass versus asymmetric block by block.

label.description: Empty until a comparison has been made.

asymmetricBlocks.description: How many separate public-key operations the payload would need.

ratio.description: How many times slower the asymmetric route would be.

decision.description: blocked = an attack was stopped; exposed = somebody who should not read this can.

reason.description: Technical code for the refusal or the exposure; null when nothing went wrong.

detail.description: The offending key, payload or size; empty when not applicable.

stats.description: Running totals across the whole run.

failed.description: Operations refused - a wrong key, an oversized payload, a broken signature.

exposed.description: Messages a third party could read. Every one of them is a key-management failure, not a cipher failure.
